_readme: Small config the agent reads/writes each run. artifactUrl is filled in after the first successful publish and must be reused (not regenerated) on every subsequent run so updates land on the same page instead of creating a new one each day.
pagesPublishScope: every run — uses GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN if set (scheduled cloud runs), else the local gh CLI
lastRunStatus: Weekly research run. No evidenceScore changes; four opportunities updated with new evidence. (1) it-teams-need-product-management-discipline-for-ai (score 3, unchanged): sixth consecutive run targeting the Product Management gap, and the first to land genuinely new admissible material -- a second HBR piece on an emerging 'agent manager' role (co-author has a disclosed Salesforce Agentforce COI, reliability scored a point below the HBR default) and a BCG piece on product teams owning AI-sales-agent content/guardrails. corroborationBreadth moved 3->4 (third independent institution) but evidenceScore arithmetic stayed at 3 since evidenceStrength is unchanged. Merged into the existing opportunity rather than founding a new one (rubric 9 near-duplicate check). (2) ai-compresses-engineering-team-size-junior-pipeline stayed at 4: added Bain's 'Half-Finished Redesign' (AI Org Assessment Survey 2026, n=155) as a sixth independent institution -- pyramid structures 66%->29% in two years, pods of 3-5, junior engineers down from ~1/3 to <1/5 of teams. (3) ai-spine-cross-functional-operating-model stayed at 4: same Bain report added as a distinct data point -- structural redesign is running well ahead of decision-rights/accountability redesign, a quantified instance of the operating-model-not-tooling root cause. (4) entry-level-hiring-contraction-mixed-evidence stayed at 4, contested: added a second Census working paper (CES-WP-26-56, 'Graduating into Disruption,' PSEO/LEHD-linked) corroborating from the college-major angle -- 5pp lower initial-employment likelihood, 13% lower initial earnings for the most AI-exposed majors. Red-teamed all thirteen evidenceScore>=4 opportunities; one notable judgment call: a Beijing arXiv wage-exposure study (DiD design) cleared the reliability threshold for ai-skills-wage-premium-it-developers but was deliberately NOT added as contradicting evidence after inspection showed it measures occupational automation exposure, a different mechanism from the individual AI-skills credential premium this opportunity tracks -- forcing it in would have manufactured a downgrade from evidence that doesn't test the actual claim. No new opportunities founded. Product Management, while still only one opportunity, is now meaningfully better-evidenced (3 institutions, up from 2). QA/Test Engineering, Data Engineering, and Help Desk/IT Support were not independently targeted this run. Census BTOS, BCG, Bain, and HBR all reset to 0 consecutiveEmptyRuns on genuine new admissible findings; BLS, McKinsey, Deloitte, WEF, OECD, and MIT CISR continue climbing without a new admissible finding (CISR is five days from its announced Oct 31, 2026 closure -- flagged again in sources.json; the next run should treat it as closed and drop it from the mandatory-every-run list). GitHub Pages mirror published and verified (publish_pages.py and --verify both exited 0).
pagesTokenPermissions: fine-grained PAT, repository access limited to sdm1130/ai-it-research-tracker, Contents: Read and write (Metadata: Read-only is added automatically). Nothing else required: main has no branch protection or rulesets, and Pages is build_type=legacy on main:/ so it rebuilds on push.

pagesPublishExitCodes.3: no credentials — skip and report mirror stale
pagesPublishExitCodes.1: real failure e.g. expired token — report loudly
